title: A 25-year-old Brazilian video patent just expired, ending a lingering legal headache for Linux
excerpt: The end of a pretty small, pretty niche era.
content_html:
Published Aug 14, 2026, 1:30 PM EDT

Simon is a Computer Science BSc graduate who has been writing about technology since 2014, and using Windows machines since 3.1. After working for an indie game studio and acting as the family's go-to technician for all computer issues, he found his passion for writing and decided to use his skill set to write about all things tech.

Since beginning his writing career, he has written for many different publications such as WorldStart, Listverse, and MakeTechEasier. However, after finding his home at MakeUseOf in February 2019, he would eventually move on to its sister site, XDA, to bring the latest and greatest in Windows, Linux, and DIY electronics.

Getting media to work on Linux is more complex than you may think. Not because of the technical aspects (although that, too, is pretty tricky), but because of the legality of distributing proprietary software and patent-encumbered codecs. While companies like Microsoft can grab a license and bake the tech into their products, it's a lot less feasible for Linux distributions designed to be freely downloaded and redistributed.

Linux developers have used workarounds for this limitation for decades now; if you've ever downloaded a Linux distro and then spent some time enabling third-party repositories to get multimedia codecs, you already know what it's like. But one patent from 2001 prevented DivX videos from being patent-free worldwide, and the good news is, it has just expired.

Siemens AG filed a patent back in 2001

Its patent family would linger for over 25 years

Our story begins back on April 9th, 2001, when Siemens AG filed the Brazilian patent BR PI0109962-0, titled "process for storing and processing image information from successive images over time." This patent was listed as part of the MPEG-4 Visual Patent Portfolio, which was administered by MPEG LA, which would later become the Via Licensing Alliance.

For years, these patents held true. In fact, in an MPEG LA PDF document from October 2025, you can see the final two unexpired patents on the very first page. The first is Dolby, which held patent BR PI0113271-7; this one expired on January 26, 2026. For the rest of 2026, the only thing stopping the tech from being patent-free worldwide was that one Siemens AG patent.

Finally, on July 19, 2026, the Siemens AG patent expired. With that patent gone, it removed the final patent obstacle preventing worldwide patent-free status.

And having no problems is better than a small problem

The reason why this was a cool milestone in the Linux community is down to how the law handles these technologies. See, Xvid is a weird case where the software is free and open-source, but there were laws covering what you could actually do with it. So yes, the Linux community had access to the software just fine, but the rights holders asked for royalties for MPEG-4 decoders and encoders sold and made in specific countries.

That's not to say that the Linux community hit a brick wall when it came to publishing Xvid support. In fact, Fedora published xvidcore back in 2023, even when the patent was still alive and kicking. But that didn't mean the Brazilian patent was worthless; it meant that people could distribute MPEG-4 Part 2 without worrying about any legal issues at all.

Not much will change for Linux users or with MP4 patent laws

You probably won't notice anything different if you're outside Brazil

So does this mean that every single MP4 file has now broken free of its patent prison? Well, no. This specific patent covered MPEG-4 Part 2. The videos we watch on modern systems using H.264/AVC tech are running off MPEG-4 Part 10, and that is still very much covered by patents. So, yeah, the Linux community isn't free to take the MP4 format and run with it wherever it pleases.

However, this does mark the end of a hanging legal issue that has finally come to an end a quarter of a century after it was set. It may not revolutionise the Linux scene, and you may not even notice that anything changes in your daily workflow, but it's a cool insight as to how the open-source community has to work around these restrictions.

Brazil's MPEG-4 Part 2 patent didn't change a lot, but it's still good that it's gone

At the end of the day, Brazil's patent didn't do a whole lot to stymie Linux. Distros like Fedora distributed the codex anyway, and it didn't come under fire with legal issues. However, it is an interesting insight into how a single patent made 25 years ago can act as a minor headache to the open-source community 25 years down the line.

content_html_zh:
发布于 2026 年 8 月 14 日下午 1:30（美国东部时间）

Simon 是一名计算机科学学士学位毕业生，自 2014 年以来一直在撰写有关技术的文章，并从 3.1 开始使用 Windows 机器。 在一家独立游戏工作室工作并担任家庭所有计算机问题的首席技术人员后，他发现了自己对写作的热情，并决定利用自己的技能来撰写有关技术的所有内容。

自开始写作生涯以来，他为许多不同的出版物撰写文章，例如 WorldStart、Listverse 和 MakeTechEasier。 然而，在 2019 年 2 月在 PCPC.me 找到自己的家后，他最终转向其姊妹网站 XDA，带来 Windows、Linux 和 DIY 电子产品方面的最新、最好的内容。

让媒体在 Linux 上运行比您想象的要复杂。 不是因为技术方面（尽管这也相当棘手），而是因为分发专有软件和受专利保护的编解码器的合法性。 虽然像微软这样的公司可以获得许可证并将技术融入到他们的产品中，但对于旨在免费下载和重新分发的 Linux 发行版来说，这不太可行。

几十年来，Linux 开发人员一直在使用解决此限制的方法。如果您曾经下载过 Linux 发行版，然后花了一些时间启用第三方存储库来获取多媒体编解码器，您就会知道它是什么样的。 但 2001 年的一项专利阻止了 DivX 视频在全球范围内免专利，好消息是它刚刚过期。

西门子股份公司早在 2001 年就申请了专利

其专利族将持续超过 25 年

我们的故事要从 2001 年 4 月 9 日开始，当时西门子股份公司提交了巴西专利 BR PI0109962-0，标题为“随时间推移存储和处理连续图像中的图像信息的过程”。 该专利被列为 MPEG-4 视觉专利组合的一部分，由 MPEG LA（后来成为 Via 许可联盟）管理。

多年来，这些专利一直有效。 事实上，在 2025 年 10 月的 MPEG LA PDF 文档中，您可以在第一页看到最后两项未过期的专利。 第一个是杜比，拥有专利BR PI0113271-7；该有效期已于 2026 年 1 月 26 日到期。 在 2026 年剩下的时间里，唯一阻止该技术在全球范围内实现无专利的就是西门子股份公司的一项专利。

最终，2026年7月19日，西门子股份公司专利到期。 随着该专利的消失，它消除了阻止全球无专利地位的最后专利障碍。

没有问题比有小问题要好

这是 Linux 社区中一个很酷的里程碑，原因在于法律如何处理这些技术。 你看，Xvid 是一个奇怪的例子，该软件是免费和开源的，但有法律规定你实际上可以用它做什么。 所以，是的，Linux 社区可以很好地访问该软件，但权利持有者要求对在特定国家/地区销售和制造的 MPEG-4 解码器和编码器收取版税。

这并不是说 Linux 社区在发布 Xvid 支持时遇到了障碍。 事实上，Fedora 早在 2023 年就发布了 xvidcore，当时该专利仍然有效。 但这并不意味着巴西专利毫无价值；这意味着人们可以分发 MPEG-4 Part 2，而无需担心任何法律问题。

对于 Linux 用户或 MP4 专利法来说不会有太大改变

如果您不在巴西，您可能不会注意到任何不同

那么这是否意味着每个 MP4 文件现在都已经摆脱了专利牢笼呢？ 嗯，不。 该特定专利涵盖了 MPEG-4 第 2 部分。 我们在使用 H.264/AVC 技术的现代系统上观看的视频正在运行 MPEG-4 第 10 部分，并且这仍然受到专利的保护。 所以，是的，Linux 社区不能自由地采用 MP4 格式并随心所欲地使用它。

然而，这确实标志着悬而未决的法律问题的结束，该问题在提出四分之一个世纪后终于得到了解决。 它可能不会彻底改变 Linux 场景，您甚至可能没有注意到日常工作流程发生任何变化，但对于开源社区如何解决这些限制，这是一个很酷的见解。

巴西的MPEG-4 Part 2专利没有太大变化，但没了还是好的

归根结底，巴西的专利并没有对 Linux 产生太大的阻碍。 不管怎样，像 Fedora 这样的发行版还是分发了该法典，而且它并没有因为法律问题而受到攻击。 然而，这是一个有趣的见解，说明 25 年前获得的一项专利如何在 25 年后成为开源社区的一个小问题。
